windowpane-test.caption: Stretch a piece of dough thin. If light shows through without it tearing, the gluten is developed.

stretch-and-fold.alt: Line drawing illustrating stretch and fold
stretch-and-fold.caption: Grab one side, stretch it up, and fold it over the top. Turn the bowl and repeat.

coil-fold.caption: Lift from the middle so both ends hang, then let them tuck under as you set it down.

slap-and-fold.alt: Line drawing illustrating slap and fold
slap-and-fold.caption: Lift, slap the far end down, fold the rest over. Wet dough tightens fast this way.

scoring.caption: A shallow cut at a low angle tells the loaf where to open.

ear.caption: The raised flap of crust along the score, lifted by oven spring.

shaping.caption: Tension on the surface, seam on the bottom. That skin is what holds the rise.

pre-shape.caption: A loose round first lets the dough relax before the final shape.

poke-test.caption: A floured finger dent that fills back slowly is a loaf ready to bake.

lamination.caption: Alternating layers of dough and butter, folded over and over.

braiding.caption: Outside strand over the middle, alternating sides.

autolyse.caption: Flour and water, rested before salt and leaven go in.

tangzhong.caption: A cooked flour paste that holds extra water for a softer, longer-lasting crumb.

bulk-fermentation.caption: The first rise, measured by how much the whole mass grows.

oven-spring.caption: The fast rise in the first minutes of baking, before the crust sets.

oven-steam.caption: Steam keeps the crust soft long enough for the loaf to finish expanding.

cold-proof.caption: A long, cold final rise in the fridge builds flavor and makes scoring easier.

float-test.caption: A spoonful that floats is full of gas. One that sinks may still be ready.

crumb.caption: The inside of the loaf: its holes, texture and tenderness.

dense-crumb.caption: Tight and heavy, usually from too little fermentation or weak gluten.

gummy-crumb.caption: A wet, sticky band, often from cutting too soon or underbaking.

fools-crumb.caption: A few giant holes with dense crumb around them: underfermented, not open.

tunneling.caption: A long cavity under the crust, usually from trapped gas during shaping.

flying-crust.caption: The top crust separates and lifts away from the crumb below it.

pancaking.caption: The loaf spreads sideways in the oven instead of rising up.

blowout.caption: The crust bursts where it was not scored, because the gas found its own exit.

overproofed.caption: Risen past its peak. The gluten is tired and the loaf will sink or spread.

underproofed.caption: Not enough rise yet. Bake it now and you get a tight, dense crumb.

boule.caption: A round loaf, from the French word for ball.

batard.caption: An oval loaf, shorter and fatter than a baguette.

baguette.caption: A long, thin loaf with a crackly crust, scored on the diagonal.

banneton.caption: The coiled basket that supports the dough during its final rise.

lame.caption: A razor blade on a handle, made for scoring dough.

dutch-oven.caption: A heavy lidded pot that traps steam from the dough itself.

bench-scraper.caption: A flat blade for dividing, lifting and shaping dough on the counter.

digital-scale.caption: Weigh everything in grams. Cups are a guess.

probe-thermometer.caption: Read the inside temperature to know the loaf is actually done.

grain-mill.caption: Turns whole wheat berries into fresh flour at home.

aliquot-jar.caption: A small straight-sided sample of dough that shows the true percentage rise.

sourdough-starter.caption: A living culture of flour, water, wild yeast and bacteria that leavens bread.

hydration.caption: Water as a percentage of flour weight. 750 g water on 1,000 g flour is 75%.

bakers-percentage.caption: Every ingredient expressed as a percent of the flour, which is always 100%.

gluten.caption: The stretchy protein network that traps gas and gives bread its structure.

wheat-berry.caption: The whole kernel: bran outside, endosperm inside, germ at the base.

proofing.caption: The final rise after shaping, right before the oven.

kneading.caption: Working the dough by hand to build gluten strength.
